quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Put a fingertip on your throat and say the word slowly. At the moment of the middle consonant, is anything different from the vowels around it?
quests.explanation: 'Pleasant' has /z/ in the middle, spelled S. Between the stressed vowel and the weak syllable that follows, voicing carries on without a break. The other candidate has the same tongue position but switches the voice off, which would make 'plessant'. The two differ only in voicing, so your throat is the best detector.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'pleh', keep your tongue tip near the ridge with your voice running and let a buzz pass over it before the weak 'unt'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the word and hold the stressed vowel as long as you can. Is the vowel before the middle consonant roomy or clipped?
quests.explanation: 'Major' has /dʒ/ in the middle: a seal, then a voiced hush. /tʃ/ shares the seal and the hush but not the voice, and would give 'matcher'. Voice also stretches the vowel before it, so the 'ay' in 'major' is longer than in 'matcher'.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the long 'ay' a moment, then bring the tongue front to the roof just behind the ridge, voice on, and release it as a buzzing hush before the quick 'er'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Imagine a recording with the vowels cut out and only the target sound left. Would there be a hum in it?
quests.explanation: 'Fashion' has /ʃ/ in the middle, spelled SH. Its voiced partner would make the word 'fazhun'. The tongue and lips take the same shape for both; only the voicing changes, and /ʃ/ is the one with none.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'fa', pull the tongue slightly back, round your lips, and hush air through with no voice before the weak 'un'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Notice where in your mouth the contact happens as the middle stop is made. Is it near the front teeth, or far back near your throat?
quests.explanation: 'Magazine' has /g/ after the first syllable. /g/ and /d/ are both voiced stops, so voicing can't help; the contact point does. /g/ closes at the back of the tongue, while /d/ closes at the tongue tip and would give 'madazine'.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ma', lift the back of your tongue to the soft palate with voice on, release into the weak 'uh', and stress the final 'zeen'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: At the middle stop, check your lips in a mirror. Do they take part?
quests.explanation: 'Tablet' has /b/ in the middle, made with both lips. /d/ would use the tongue tip instead and give 'tadlet'. Both are voiced stops, so the lip closure is the thing to look for.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ta', close both lips with voice on and release into the weak 'lit'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and freeze at the middle consonant. Is the tip of your tongue involved, or only the back?
quests.explanation: 'Rocket' has /k/ in the middle, with the back of the tongue against the soft palate, followed by a weak syllable ending in /t/. Using the tongue tip for the middle would give 'rottet'. The /t/ at the end is a separate sound.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'rock', keep the back of your tongue closed for 'k', release quickly into 'it', and finish with the tongue-tip 't'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The nasal comes right before a hiss. Hold the nasal and notice where your tongue is touching.
quests.explanation: 'Pencil' has /n/ in the middle, with the tongue tip on the ridge, just where the following /s/ is made, so the tongue barely moves. /ŋ/ would raise the back of the tongue and give 'pengsil'.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'pe', touch your tongue tip to the ridge and hum through your nose, then release into the hiss of 'sil'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: A K sound follows the nasal. Where is your tongue when the K is released?
quests.explanation: 'Uncle' has /ŋ/ in the middle: the back of the tongue is already raised for the /k/ that follows, so the nasal is made there too. A tongue-tip /n/ would add an extra movement and give 'un-kle' with a hesitation.
quests.mouthPosition: Begin with a relaxed vowel, raise the back of the tongue to hum, then release into 'k' with a puff and glide into 'ul'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Compare the final sound with the nasal in the middle of the word. Which of them lets air flow around the sides of the tongue?
quests.explanation: 'Channel' has /n/ in the middle and /l/ at the end. The /l/ keeps air in the mouth and lets it flow around the sides of the tongue, while the nasal sends air through the nose. Ending with /n/ would give 'channen'.
quests.mouthPosition: End by touching the tongue tip to the ridge, sides of the tongue lowered, voice on.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the middle sound alone and hold it. Where is the tongue tip: behind the teeth, or touching them?
quests.explanation: 'Other' has /ð/ in the middle, with the tongue tip touching the back of the upper teeth. /z/ is also voiced, but the tongue stays behind the teeth and would give 'uzzer'. Place of articulation is the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: After the first vowel, the tongue tip just touches the back of the upper teeth; keep the voice going so the air hums through the gap.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Use a mirror. When the middle sound is made, can you see your tongue?
quests.explanation: 'Athlete' has /θ/ in the middle: the tongue tip slides forward between the teeth with no voice. /s/ is also voiceless, but the tongue stays behind the teeth and would give 'asslete'. Both are hisses, so place decides.
quests.mouthPosition: Straight after the stressed 'a', slide your tongue tip between your teeth for the soft voiceless 'th', then pull it back for 'leet'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Compare the middle sound with the last sound of the word 'cloth'. Does it match, or differ?
quests.explanation: 'Clothing' has /ð/ in the middle, voiced, unlike the /θ/ at the end of 'cloth'. The tongue position is identical and the vowel changes too. A voiceless middle would make it sound like 'cloth-ing' with a stiff break.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'kloh', rest your tongue tip against the back of your upper teeth, voice on, and glide into 'ing'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The target follows a lip-teeth hiss. Does your tongue tip touch anything as the sound is made?
quests.explanation: 'Afraid' has /r/ in the cluster after /f/: the tongue is pulled back without touching the ridge. Touching it would give /l/ and 'aflaid'. It's the same /fr/ you practised at the start of words, now in the middle.
quests.mouthPosition: After the weak 'uh', rest your top teeth on your bottom lip for 'f', then pull your tongue back for 'r' and open into 'ayd'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Pay attention to the sides of your tongue as you make the middle sound. Is air passing around them?
quests.explanation: 'Alone' has /l/ after the weak first syllable: the tongue tip touches the ridge and air flows around the sides. Pulling the tongue back gives /r/ and 'a-rone'.
quests.mouthPosition: Once the weak 'uh' is said, press your tongue tip on the ridge with voice on, then open into 'ohn'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Look at your lips in a mirror at the middle consonant. Do they round, or does the lip meet your teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Reward' has /w/ after the weak 're': the lips round and open into the stressed vowel. /v/ would put the lip on the teeth and give 'reverd'. Rounded lips with no contact is what defines /w/.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ri', round your lips tightly and spring them open into 'ord', finishing with 'd'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The target is a lip stop. Does your voice stay on right up to the moment the lips open?
quests.explanation: 'Obvious' has /b/ before /v/: /ˈɒbviəs/. Two voiced sounds sit side by side, so the buzz carries through. Making the /b/ voiceless gives 'opvious'.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ob', close both lips with voice on, release into the lip-teeth buzz of 'v', and finish with 'ee-us'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the word and stop right after the first syllable. What does the stressed syllable start with?
quests.explanation: 'Disease' has /z/ at the start of the stressed syllable, spelled S: /dɪˈziːz/. It's voiced, as is the final /z/. Using /s/ would make 'dissease'. The two ends of the stressed syllable match.
quests.mouthPosition: Following the weak 'di', put your tongue tip near the ridge with voice on and buzz into the stressed 'zeez'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: A tongue-tip stop sits just before the target. Does the lip-teeth contact come with or without voice?
quests.explanation: 'Advantage' has /v/ after /d/: /ədˈvæntɪdʒ/. The target is voiced, like the /d/ before it. Making it /f/ gives 'adfantage'. Words with the prefix ad- tempt a voiceless second sound.
quests.mouthPosition: Right after the tongue-tip 'd', swing your lower lip up to your upper teeth and buzz into 'van-tij'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The spelling ends in -dge. Say the final sound and check what comes before the hush: does the seal carry voice?
quests.explanation: 'Knowledge' ends in /dʒ/: /ˈnɒlɪdʒ/. The K is silent at the start; the ending is a voiced seal-and-hush. /tʃ/ would give 'nolich', which drops the voice.
quests.mouthPosition: At the end, let the tongue front rise to the roof behind the ridge with the voice still running, and release it as a short buzzing hush.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Hold the stressed vowel as long as you can. Then add the ending. Does the ending bring voice with it?
quests.explanation: 'Approach' ends in /tʃ/: a quick seal and a voiceless hush. A voiced ending would sound like 'approje'. The spelling -ch is /tʃ/ at the end of many words, including 'teach', 'reach' and 'beach'.
quests.mouthPosition: Straight after the 'oh' glide, seal your tongue behind the ridge with voice off and release a short hush.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the final sound by itself. Does the air stop at any moment before it flows?
quests.explanation: 'Brush' ends in /ʃ/: continuous airflow with no closure. Adding a stop gives 'brutch'. The word begins with a cluster, but the ending is a simple hush.
quests.mouthPosition: After the short 'u', pull your tongue slightly back, round your lips, and let a steady hush finish the word.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Set the last letters, GH, aside. Does the final sound let your voice continue?
quests.explanation: 'Tough' ends in /f/ even though the spelling ends in GH. The lip-teeth hiss is voiceless. /v/ would give 'tuv'. The vowel is short before a voiceless ending.
quests.mouthPosition: Once the short 'u' is said, rest your top teeth on your bottom lip and blow a voiceless stream of air.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Notice whether your lips close completely at the end of the word.
quests.explanation: 'Above' ends in /v/: the lip touches the teeth and the voice buzzes through a narrow gap. /b/ would seal both lips and give 'abub'. The word has /b/ in the second syllable too, so the two consonants should sound different.
quests.mouthPosition: To end the word, lift the lower lip to the upper teeth and keep the voice buzzing until you stop.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the final sound and compare it with the one at the end of 'breathe'. Are they the same?
quests.explanation: 'Teeth' ends in /θ/: voiceless. The verb 'teethe' ends in /ð/. Both place the tongue between the teeth; only voice differs. The vowel is also shorter in 'teeth' than in 'teethe'.
quests.mouthPosition: Following the long 'ee', slide your tongue tip between your teeth and let a soft voiceless stream of air pass.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: There's a silent letter in this word. After it, what does the next consonant do to your voice?
quests.explanation: 'Christmas' has /s/ in the middle, followed by /m/: /ˈkrɪsməs/. The T is silent. Voicing the /s/ gives 'Chrizmas'. Both /s/ sounds in the word are voiceless.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'kri', hiss with your tongue tip near the ridge and no voice, then close your lips for 'm'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The letter X stands for two sounds in this word. The second one is the target. Does it carry voice?
quests.explanation: 'Exist' has /z/ in the middle: /ɪgˈzɪst/. X is /gz/ here, and the /z/ is voiced, matching the /g/ before it. Using /s/ gives 'eksist'. The ending /st/ is a separate voiceless cluster.
quests.mouthPosition: Straight after the weak 'ig', put your tongue tip near the ridge with voice on and buzz into 'zist'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: There's a silent letter in the middle. At the end, which closure is it: the lips or the tongue tip?
quests.explanation: 'Debt' ends in /t/; the B is silent. Saying a /b/ gives 'debbt'. The silent B comes from the word's Latin origin; it's one of several to memorise, with 'doubt' and 'subtle'.
quests.mouthPosition: After the short 'e', close the tongue tip against the ridge for a silent 't'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Pick up the first sound and hold it. Does your throat vibrate while the tongue is at the teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Thorough' begins with /θ/, voiceless. /ð/ is the voiced version, which opens function words like 'the' but not words like this one. Starting with /ð/ gives 'dhorough'. The voice stays off at the start.
quests.mouthPosition: Place your tongue tip lightly between your teeth, blow a soft voiceless stream of air, and glide into 'ur-uh'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Cover your ears with your hands and hold the middle sound. How loud is it inside your head?
quests.explanation: 'Vision' has /ʒ/ in the middle, voiced. /ʃ/ would give 'vishion'. The tongue and lips are in identical positions for both; only the voice differs.
quests.mouthPosition: Pull the tongue back a little and round the lips as for a hush, but keep the voice buzzing all the way through.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: There's a silent letter at the end. Do the lips pop open, or stay together with a hum?
quests.explanation: 'Bomb' ends in /m/; the B is silent. The word begins with /b/, so the written B appears twice but is heard only once. Close the lips and hum to finish.
quests.mouthPosition: Once the 'o' is said, close both lips and let the hum run through your nose.
